details: Agentic LLM systems assume natural language as the universal communication interface, so domain-specific scientific foundation models (time series, tabular, etc.) that lack native language I/O cannot participate in agentic reasoning.
Serializing structured scientific data into tokens is both inaccurate and token-expensive.

Eywa: a heterogeneous agentic framework in which a domain-specific foundation model is bonded to an LLM through a bidirectional 'Tsaheylu' interface — a query compiler mapping the agent's language state to a structured FM invocation, and a response adapter mapping FM output back into language-consumable context — with the LLM deciding at each step whether to invoke or skip the FM.

Three instantiations of this primitive: EywaAgent (single coupled FM-LLM agent), EywaMAS (drop-in replacement of language agents by EywaAgents in existing multi-agent topologies), and EywaOrchestra (an LLM 'conductor' that per-task selects agent types, backbone LLMs, attached FMs, and communication topology).
Accompanying contribution: EywaBench, a multi-task/multi-domain scientific benchmark covering language, time-series, and tabular modalities under one unified utility score.
Built from existing sources including DeepPrinciple, MMLU-Pro, fev-bench (time series), and TabArena (tabular).
Three domains x three sub-domains: physical (material, energy, space), life (biology, clinic, drug), social (economy, business, infrastructure).
Unified utility score in [0,1]: soft-match for language tasks, normalized prediction error for time-series/tabular tasks; reports per-domain and overall mean utility.
Designed to scale by resampling temporal windows/variables and by adding new time-series/tabular sources.
Default LLM backbone gpt-5-nano; backbone ablation with gpt-4.1-nano and gpt-5-mini.
Foundation models: Chronos (time series) and TabPFN (tabular), neither with a native language interface.
Tsaheylu implemented with LangChain agents plus FastMCP servers; each FM served as an independent MCP endpoint over streamable HTTP, with server-side task data storage.

EywaAgent/EywaMAS use expert-assigned FM per sample (EywaMAS default = debate topology); EywaOrchestra selects FM and topology automatically; up to two retries on unparsable outputs; latency and token usage logged on a local CPU machine.
Single-agent LLM baselines across GPT, Gemini, and Claude families.
Homogeneous LLM multi-agent systems: Self-Refine and Multi-Agent Debate on the same backbone.
Heterogeneous LLM-only multi-agent systems: Mixture-of-Agents and X-MAS.
Sensitivity to LLM sampling temperature, TabPFN softmax temperature, and prompt design (Detailed vs Chain-of-Thought vs ReAct); turn ablation in appendix.

Formal setup: task input factorizes into a language-observable part and domain-specific parts; Assumption of 'domain advantage' (FM strictly beats any LLM on serialized domain input) yields Theorem that EywaAgent's function class attains strictly lower optimal risk; analogous result for EywaMAS; orchestration argued via oracle adaptive risk <= best fixed-configuration risk.
Qualitative case studies comparing a language-only agent with EywaAgent on structured financial signals and illustrating EywaOrchestra.

key_findings.finding: Bonding a foundation model to an LLM improves scientific task utility while simultaneously cutting token and time cost relative to a single language-only agent.
key_findings.evidence: On EywaBench with the same backbone, EywaAgent raises average utility by 6.6% (~7% across physical, life, and social science tasks) while reducing token usage by nearly 30% and execution time by roughly 10%.

key_findings.finding: Cross-modality heterogeneity matters more than heterogeneity among language models for scientific workloads.
key_findings.evidence: Heterogeneous LLM-only multi-agent baselines (MoA, X-MAS) do not consistently beat strong homogeneous MAS baselines on EywaBench, whereas EywaMAS achieves the best overall utility, beating Refine substantially and beating Debate in both utility and token usage under the same debate topology.

key_findings.finding: Automatic per-task orchestration nearly matches expert-configured multi-agent systems at markedly lower inference cost.
key_findings.evidence: EywaOrchestra, using no expert configuration, reaches utility close to expert-designed EywaMAS and surpasses it on several sub-domains while substantially lowering latency and token usage versus fixed multi-agent systems.

key_findings.finding: No single fixed system configuration is optimal across domains, motivating adaptive orchestration.
key_findings.evidence: In economy and business sub-domains the single-agent EywaAgent is already highly competitive with heavier multi-agent topologies; theoretically the oracle adaptive risk is at most the best fixed-configuration risk, strictly less when different task regions favor different configurations.

key_findings.finding: The framework's gains are robust to design choices and improve with stronger backbones.
key_findings.evidence: Utility of EywaAgent/EywaMAS/EywaOrchestra remains stable across LLM sampling temperatures (peaking at moderate values), TabPFN softmax temperatures, and prompt styles (with more structured prompts such as ReAct slightly better); utility trends upward from gpt-4.1-nano to gpt-5-nano to gpt-5-mini across all three science domains.
